Claim with `./hq claim 48 --agent claude`, build strictly inside the issue's Scope, run `bun install` in the worktree first, run `./hq check`, rebase on origin/main, open the PR with `./hq pr 48 --body-file .context/pr-48.md` (add --allow-dirty only for untracked generated files you deliberately did not commit; retry once if the push is rejected with commit_refs_rules), then stop and report PR number and evidence. Do not ship/merge. Run the anti-slop skill on changed UI. Health values must never be logged. Never read .env files. A local test `speak > names a missing api key from a fresh process` may fail only because of a git-ignored .env.local; say so rather than working around it.

1	---
2	name: hq-work
3	description: 'Use when a human assigns you a GitHub issue ("work on #N" or "/hq-work N"). Takes it from claim to a reviewed PR.'
4	---
5	
6	# hq-work
7	
8	`N` = issue, `<you>` = `claude`, `codex` or `cursor`, `<PR>` = PR number. Windows: `hq.cmd` for `./hq`.
9	
10	1. Claim: `./hq claim N --agent <you>`. If it refuses, stop and tell the human why. Read what it
11	   prints: the issue, work in flight, overlapping files.
12	2. Context before code. Read only the docs the issue needs, then run
13	   `entire search "<topic>"`, `entire graph query "<task>"` and `entire brain brief "<task>"`.
14	   Before rewriting code you did not write: `entire why <file>:<line>`.
15	3. Plan inline in a few bullets. No spec or plan documents.
16	4. Build inside Scope, never in "Do not touch". Small commits, staged by name:
17	   `git add <file> <file> && git commit -m "<what the product can now do>"`.
18	   Push whenever you like: `git push -u origin HEAD`.
19	5. Verify: run the issue's Verify steps, then `./hq check` until it passes.
20	6. Sync with main. Not pushed yet: `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`. Already pushed:
21	   `git fetch origin && git merge origin/main` (never force-push). Fix conflicts in your own
22	   changes, `git add <files>`, then `git rebase --continue` or `git commit`. Re-run `./hq check`.
23	7. Write `.context/pr-N.md` (template below; `mkdir -p .context` if needed), then
24	   `./hq pr N --body-file .context/pr-N.md`. It pushes, opens the PR with `Closes #N` and sets
25	   `status:review`. Get the number: `gh pr view --json number,url`.
26	8. Trail: Entire opens a trail for your PR by itself. Check it with `entire trail show`, then run `entire trail ci-pr` (safe to re-run). Only if `trail show` finds none: `entire trail create --title "<issue title> (#N)" --type feature`.
27	9. Review, unless the issue is `size:S`: `entire review`. Fix real findings, commit, `git push`,
28	   re-run `./hq check`. Then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass` and `entire trail ready`.
29	10. Report the PR link, check result and risks, then stop. Merge only on "ship it" (`/hq-ship`).
30	
31	PR body template for `.context/pr-N.md`:
32	
33	````markdown
34	## What changed
35	- <what the product can now do>
36	
37	## How verified
38	- <Verify steps you ran and what you saw>
39	```
40	<tail of ./hq check>
41	```
42	
43	## Risks
44	- <what could break, or "none">
45	
46	## Screenshots
47	<UI changes only, else "n/a">
48	````
49	
50	Out of scope: do not do it. Write `.context/new-issue.md` with the headings `### Goal`,
51	`### Acceptance criteria`, `### Scope`, `### Do not touch`, `### Blocked by`, `### Verify`,
52	`### Notes` (say "Found while working on #N" in Notes), then
53	`gh issue create --title "<title>" --body-file .context/new-issue.md --label status:needs-human`.
54	Link it on your issue: `gh issue comment N --body "Follow-up: #M"`. Carry on with your own scope.
55	
56	Stuck (unclear criteria, waiting on another issue, a conflict in code you did not write):
57	`./hq release N --needs-human --note "<one crisp question>"`, then stop.
58	
59	Done means: every acceptance criterion met, `./hq check` passes with its tail in the PR, PR open
60	with evidence, `review:pass` (unless `size:S`).
61

### Goal

The server keeps every night: dense series in Tiger, one summary per night in MongoDB.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Migrations `*_night_*.sql`: `night_noise` and `vitals` hypertables, `sleep_stages` table
- [ ] `night.upload` validates `NightUpload`, writes series and the summary document, idempotent on `nightId`
- [ ] Health series stored only when `consent.health` is true; location only with location consent
- [ ] `night.get` and `night.list`; service exports for other features: `getNight`, `addEventLabels`, `setAttribution`, `setEvidence`, `deleteUserNights`
- [ ] Tests with the upload fixture and mocked repos

- `apps/server/src/features/night/`
- `packages/shared/src/night/`
- `apps/server/src/db/migrations/*_night_*.sql` (new files)

content.thinking:
I'm planning the design as two files: a pure, streaming-friendly parser module and a separate CLI that drives it. Since the export XML can run to hundreds of megabytes, I'll read it line by line from a Bun file stream, relying on the fact that each Apple `<Record>` sits on a single line. Now I'm turning to the record types I need to handle, starting with sleep analysis.

I'm mapping the Apple sleep stage values onto my own categories: in-bed, awake, core, deep and REM, with unspecified asleep falling back to core. I also need the heart rate, HRV and respiratory rate units, and the date format that converts to ISO with an offset, and I'm weighing how to define the night window from the sleep stage span.

I need to check whether the service accepts an empty noise array and how Lnight is computed without it. I'll look at `service.uploadNight`, since the script has to post through tRPC with the `API_URL` env and `--user`, and the server's superjson transformer means the body goes out as `{"json": input}`. That should be enough to decide whether I can use plain `fetch` without superjson.

content.thinking:
I'm settling on a deterministic night ID built from the user and the night, so reruns are idempotent, and I'm hashing it with sha256 and setting the version and variant bits so it validates as a UUID. Mic consent is false, so the noise is ignored and the samples can be empty. Now I'm writing the parser.

I'm moving on to the CLI, tests, and README, and I'm checking that the shared domain can be imported from the server. The seed already uses it, so I'll assume it works. For parsing, I'll pull attributes from each `<Record` line with a regex, and I don't need to unescape XML since the fields I read don't use entities. For the night itself, I'll keep it simple: take `--night` as required, and use a two-pass approach to collect candidate records and then trim them to the sleep window. I'll only report counts in the CLI so no health values get logged.
